ai.title: Add docs center, downgrade drizzle-orm, switch to Bun
ai.summary: New docs center added via Contentlayer and MDX in `web/`. `drizzle-orm` downgraded 0.38.0 to 0.36.4 in `common/package.json`. Schema callbacks in `common/src/db/schema.ts` shifted from object to array returns for `primaryKey` and `index`. Docs surface covers `web/src/app/docs/`, `web/contentlayer.config.ts`, and `web/next.config.mjs`. `knowledge.md` mandates Bun for package management.

eli5.text: You can now find a full documentation center on the website, where articles are written in an extended Markdown format and organized by category in the sidebar. Behind the scenes, the database layer was rolled back to an earlier version of its ORM tool and the project switched to using Bun for all package management tasks. The sidebar on the docs pages can be opened, closed, and pinned with a keyboard shortcut, and your open or collapsed preference is remembered via a cookie. Because the site now rebuilds documentation from source files at build time, a new generated cache folder appears and is ignored by version control.

ai.title: Add Gemini API integration
ai.summary: New backend/src/gemini-api.ts implements promptGemini using OpenAI SDK against Google's generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai endpoint. GEMINI_API_KEY env var added to backend/src/env.mjs with AI prefix validation. common/src/constants.ts exposes geminiModels mapping gemini2flash to gemini-2.0-flash-exp, merged into unified models export. Responses tracked via saveMessage with Helicone headers for fingerprinting and cost attribution.

eli5.text: The assistant can now connect to Google's Gemini model in addition to the ones already supported. If you looked at the settings, you'd see a new option for a Google-based AI alongside the existing choices. A secret key for Google's service was also added to the system's configuration, and usage of the new model is being logged for tracking and billing purposes.

ai.title: Add unhandledRejection handler to backend
ai.summary: Added `unhandledRejection` handler to `backend/src/index.ts` to log errors without crashing the server. Updated `uncaughtException` handler to include structured logging and console output. Scope limited to backend process management.

eli5.text: When something goes wrong behind the scenes in the backend system, the application now records the problem and keeps running instead of crashing silently or taking the whole service down. This affects anyone using the backend services, as the system will stay more stable during unexpected failures. If you were monitoring server uptime, you would notice fewer unplanned interruptions, because errors that previously caused crashes are now caught and logged, allowing the system to continue operating.

ai.title: Add cost/quality mode selection
ai.summary: Added --mode flag (cheap/normal/expensive) to CLI. Backend selects Claude models via getModelForMode based on mode and operation type. Cheap mode skips non-obvious/test/config file requests, using only key files. Affects npm-app, backend prompts, and common constants.

eli5.text: You can now choose how much money you want to spend versus how good the answer is by picking cheap, normal, or expensive. A cheaper mode uses a faster, cheaper AI model and only looks at fewer files, while the expensive option uses a more powerful model and considers more files, giving better quality results at a higher cost. This setting works whether you're asking the assistant to do a task or to figure out which files are relevant, and it's available now when you interact with the tool.

ai.title: Added Substack news feed to docs sidebar and footer
ai.summary: Added `https://news.codebuff.com` to the docs sidebar and site footer. Implemented a serverless route `web/src/app/api/feed/route.ts` to fetch and parse the Substack RSS feed into JSON. The `DocSidebar` component now dynamically loads these articles via `getNewsArticles` in `web/src/lib/docs.ts`, rendering them under a new 'News' section with external links.

eli5.text: You can now see the latest CodeBuff news articles directly in the documentation sidebar and site footer. When you open the docs, a new 'News' section appears under the sidebar with links that take you to the full articles on Substack. The site also pulls in the RSS feed through a background connection so the list stays updated automatically, without anyone having to paste in new links by hand.

ai.title: Lowercase sponsee param in web page
ai.summary: Sponsee name extraction in web/src/app/[sponsee]/page.tsx now applies toLowerCase() to the route param. This ensures case-insensitive matching for sponsee profiles. Change scoped to the web app's dynamic route handler.

eli5.text: When you open a sponsor's profile page at /sponsee/someones-name, the app used to care about capitalization. Now it quietly converts the name to lowercase before looking it up, so /sponsee/JohnDoe and /sponcee/johndoe both show the same profile. You'll notice this if you paste a link with mixed-case letters into your browser and the page still loads the right sponsor without a 404. It affects anyone clicking or sharing links to sponsor pages on the web app, which is live today.

ai.title: Propagate mode to request files prompt
ai.summary: Mode parameter added to `requestRelevantFiles` and `getFileVersionUpdates` in `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. `countPerRequest` varies by mode: 6 for expensive, 7 for cheap, 5 for normal. `generateFileRequests` skips example prompt generation in cheap mode. `mode` default removed from `mainPrompt` signature, requiring explicit propagation via `websocket-action.ts`.

eli5.text: You told us what to do, and the computer now asks for more files at a time from the expensive model, fewer from the cheap one, while skipping extra setup in cheap mode to save work. The change is live today: any time the system needs more files to read, it now adjusts how it asks based on the mode you're running, and it always needs that mode specified before it can even start.

ai.title: Replace --mode flag with --cheap and --expensive in CLI
ai.summary: The CLI mode selection now uses boolean flags `--cheap` and `--expensive` instead of the value-based `--mode <cheap|normal|expensive>` argument. This simplifies argument parsing in `npm-app/src/index.ts` by removing the need for an index lookup and value validation step, defaulting to 'normal' if neither flag is present. The change is scoped to the `npm-app` package entry point and updates the help text to describe the specific model quality and file fetch behavior for each flag.

eli5.text: The command you type to run Codebuff now uses simple yes/no switches instead of picking an option from a menu. Instead of typing --mode expensive (which picks a quality level and fetches more files), you now just type the flag --cheap for the budget-friendly but lower-quality option, or --expensive for the higher-quality option that examines more of your project. This only affects how you interact with Codebuff's command-line tool; the underlying behavior of each setting stays the same.
